ord-page-desc: Provincial ordinances of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon
ord-what-is-p1: A provincial ordinance is a local law enacted by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (Provincial Board) and approved by the Governor, or passed over the Governor's veto. It has the force of law throughout Bukidnon, within the powers the Local Government Code gives provinces.
ord-what-is-p2: Provincial ordinances commonly cover provincial taxes, fees and charges; the annual and supplemental budgets (appropriation ordinances); provincial offices and programs; and provincial property, roads and facilities. Business permits, public markets and tricycle franchises are covered by city and municipal ordinances instead.
reso-page-desc: Resolutions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon
reso-what-is-p1: A resolution is a formal expression of the opinion or will of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on a specific matter. Unlike an ordinance, it is generally not a law; it records the Board's position or decision.
reso-what-is-p2: Provincial resolutions are used for commendations, requests to national agencies, expressions of support or opposition, authorizing the Governor to sign agreements, adopting plans, and acting on the review of city and municipal ordinances.
leg-committee-conducts-public-hearing-an: The committee studies the measure and may hold public hearings. A public hearing is required before a tax ordinance is enacted (LGC Sec. 187).
leg-committee-reviews-and-approves-the-p: The committee concerned reviews it. Some resolutions are taken up directly in session when the internal rules allow.
leg-committee-submits-findings-and-recom: The committee reports its findings and recommendation to the full Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
leg-detailed-discussion-and-debate-on-th: Members debate the proposed ordinance and propose amendments.
leg-expressions-of-the-legislative-bodys: Expressions of the legislative body's will or opinion on specific matters, often used for commendations, requests, or policy positions.
leg-final-voting-on-the-proposed-ordinan: The Sanggunian votes on the final text. A quorum (a majority of all members) must be present.
leg-initial-reading-and-assignment-to-th: The title is read in session and the measure is referred to the committee concerned.
leg-learn-about-the-legislative-process-: Learn about the legislative process of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan
leg-local-laws-with-permanent-and-genera: Local laws of general and lasting application. Provincial ordinances apply throughout Bukidnon, within the powers the Local Government Code gives provinces.
leg-provincial-ordinances-enacted-by-the: Provincial ordinances: local laws passed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and approved by the Governor that apply across Bukidnon.
leg-ordinance-takes-effect-and-is-enforc: Unless it states otherwise, the ordinance takes effect 10 days after posting (LGC Sec. 59) and is enforced across the province.
leg-ordinances-and-resolutions-of-the-sa: How the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Bukidnon makes provincial ordinances and resolutions
leg-public-posting-and-publication-of-th: Within 5 days of approval, it is posted at the Provincial Capitol entrance and in at least two other conspicuous places. The gist of an ordinance with penalties is published in a newspaper of general circulation in the province.
leg-resolution-is-posted-publicly-and-tr: Resolution is posted publicly and transmitted to concerned parties
leg-resolution-is-scheduled-for-inclusio: Resolution is scheduled for inclusion in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan session
leg-secretary-to-the-sanggunian-and-pres: The Secretary to the Sanggunian attests it and the Vice Governor certifies it. Resolutions adopting a development plan or public investment program are also subject to the Governor's approval.
leg-stepbystep-process-for-enacting-ordi: How a provincial ordinance or resolution is passed under the Local Government Code. Details follow the Sanggunian's internal rules.
leg-submit-the-proposed-ordinance-to-the: A board member files the proposed ordinance with the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. The Governor may also propose measures.
leg-submit-the-proposed-resolution-to-th: A board member files the proposed resolution with the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
leg-resolutions-passed-by-the-sp: Resolutions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan: formal statements of the Board's position or decision on a specific matter.
leg-members-desc: The provincial board is the Province's legislative body. It is made up of the Vice Governor as presiding officer, 10 board members elected by district, and 4 ex officio members.
leg-presiding-officer-desc: The Vice Governor presides over sessions and votes only to break a tie (Local Government Code, Sec. 49).
leg-ex-officio-desc: They sit because of another office they hold (Local Government Code, Sec. 467; the IPMR under the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act).
leg-members-note: Ex officio seats change when the federations elect new officers. Confirm the current membership with the Sangguniang Panlalawigan at the Provincial Capitol, Malaybalay City.
leg-presented-to-the-governor-desc: The enacted ordinance goes to the Governor, who signs each page to approve it (LGC Sec. 54).
leg-governor-approval-or-veto-desc: The Governor may veto it in writing within 15 days if it is beyond the Province's powers or harmful to public welfare. Items of an appropriation ordinance can be vetoed separately. With no action in 15 days, it is deemed approved (LGC Secs. 54–55).
leg-veto-override-desc: The Sanggunian can override a veto by a two-thirds vote of all its members. The Governor can veto a measure only once.
leg-approval-in-session-desc: Members vote on the resolution in a regular or special session.
leg-relation-desc: Bukidnon has 2 component cities and 20 municipalities. Each has its own legislative council.
leg-relation-who-desc: The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passes ordinances within the Province's powers, such as provincial taxes and fees, the provincial budget, and provincial programs and facilities. The Sangguniang Panlungsod of Malaybalay City and of Valencia City and the Sangguniang Bayan of each municipality legislate for their own city or municipality, for example on business permits, public markets and tricycle franchises.
leg-relation-review-desc: Within 3 days after approval, each city and municipal sanggunian sends the Sangguniang Panlalawigan copies of its approved ordinances and of resolutions approving local development plans and public investment programs. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan reviews them within 30 days of receipt.
leg-relation-outcome-desc: If the Sangguniang Panlalawigan finds that an ordinance goes beyond the powers of the city or municipal sanggunian, it declares the ordinance invalid in whole or in part. If it takes no action within 30 days, the ordinance is presumed consistent with law and valid.
leg-relation-barangay-desc: Barangay ordinances are reviewed by the city or municipal sanggunian, not by the Province (LGC Sec. 57). For a city, municipal or barangay ordinance, ask the city or municipal hall concerned.
leg-see-lgu-list: See the list of cities and municipalities
leg-public-participation-desc: Sanggunian sessions are open to the public unless a closed-door session is ordered by majority vote. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan holds regular sessions at least once a week (LGC Sec. 52), and residents can take part in public hearings.
leg-transparency-desc: Enacted ordinances must be posted publicly. This volunteer site does not list Bukidnon's ordinances and resolutions yet. For official copies, see bukidnon.gov.ph or ask at the Provincial Capitol.
ord-process-title: How a Provincial Ordinance Is Passed
ord-process-subtitle: The main steps under the Local Government Code (Republic Act No. 7160). Details follow the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's internal rules.
ord-step-1-desc: A board member files the proposed ordinance. It is read in session and referred to the committee concerned.
ord-step-2-desc: The committee studies the measure and may hold public hearings with the offices and sectors affected. A tax ordinance needs a public hearing before it is enacted (LGC Sec. 187).
ord-step-3-desc: Members debate and amend the measure, then vote on the final text with a quorum present.
ord-step-4-desc: The Governor signs each page to approve it, or vetoes it in writing within 15 days. With no action in 15 days, it is deemed approved (LGC Sec. 54).
ord-step-5-desc: The Sangguniang Panlalawigan may override a veto by a two-thirds vote of all its members (LGC Sec. 55).
ord-step-6-desc: Within 5 days of approval, the ordinance is posted at the Provincial Capitol and in other conspicuous places, and the gist of an ordinance with penalties is published in a newspaper of general circulation in the province. Unless it says otherwise, it takes effect 10 days after posting (LGC Sec. 59).
ord-lgu-desc: Malaybalay City, Valencia City and the 20 municipalities pass their own ordinances. Their sanggunian sends approved ordinances to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within 3 days. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan reviews them within 30 days and declares invalid any ordinance that goes beyond the city or municipal sanggunian's powers; with no action in 30 days, the ordinance is presumed valid (LGC Sec. 56).

reso-process-title: How a Provincial Resolution Is Passed
reso-process-subtitle: The usual steps at the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Details follow its internal rules.
reso-step-1-desc: A board member files the proposed resolution, and it is included in the session agenda.
reso-step-2-desc: It is referred to the committee concerned, or taken up directly in session when the internal rules allow.
reso-step-3-desc: Members vote on the resolution in session, with a quorum present.
reso-step-4-desc: The Secretary to the Sanggunian attests it and the Vice Governor, as Presiding Officer, certifies it. Resolutions adopting a development plan or public investment program are also subject to the Governor's approval.
reso-step-5-desc: Copies are sent to the offices, agencies or local governments concerned.
